textbookText: Word breakdown: A = without, MITOSIS = mitosis. So amitosis = 'without mitosis'.
Quick Test
Q1. What does 'amitosis' literally mean? → Division without mitosis (no visible chromosomes).
Q2. In which cells is it common? → Simple one-celled organisms (amoeba, some protozoans/parasites).
Q3. Are the two daughter cells genetically identical? → Yes, almost exact copies of the parent.
Q4. What is the main disadvantage of amitosis? → No error correction; mutations pass straight through to both daughters.
Fig 2.1 — Amitosis (direct division): nucleus elongates then pinches into two. No spindle, no chromosomes.
UNIT 3 — MITOSIS (Equational Division)
What Is It?

Mitosis is the main way your body makes new body cells. One parent cell (2n = diploid, 46 chromosomes in humans) divides to make two identical daughter cells, each with 2n = 46 chromosomes. It's called 'equational division' because each daughter gets an equal share of the DNA.
The 5 Stages of Mitosis
Mnemonic: 'Please Make A Toast + Cake' → P-M-A-T + C
That's the 4 stages of the nucleus (PMAT) plus cytokinesis (C) when the cell actually splits.

P — Prophase — The DNA (two sister chromatids joined at the centromere) coils up into visible X-shaped chromosomes. The nuclear membrane breaks down. Spindle fibres start forming from the two centrosomes.
M — Metaphase — All chromosomes line up in the MIDDLE of the cell (the metaphase plate). This is the best time to see all 46 chromosomes clearly. Mnemonic: 'M for Middle'.
A — Anaphase — Sister chromatids separate and are pulled to opposite poles by the spindle fibres. Each chromatid is now called a chromosome. Mnemonic: 'A for Apart' — the chromatids go apart.
T — Telophase — Two new nuclei form around the separated chromosomes at each pole. The nuclear membrane rebuilds. Chromosomes uncoil back into chromatin. Mnemonic: 'T for Two new nuclei'.

C — Cytokinesis — The cytoplasm divides. The cell pinches into two. In animal cells: a 'cleavage furrow' pinches the middle. In plant cells: a 'cell plate' builds a new wall between them. Mnemonic: 'C for Cut — the cell is cut in two'.
Why It Matters
Growth — you grow from 1 cell (zygote) to trillions via mitosis.
Repair — every cut, bruise, and broken bone heals via mitosis.
Cell replacement — skin, gut lining, and blood cells are constantly replaced via mitosis.
Mnemonic for the 5 Stages
'Please Meet Anna, Tell Charlie'
P — Prophase
M — Metaphase
A — Anaphase
T — Telophase
C — Cytokinesis
Or even simpler: 'PMAT + C' — Please Make A Toast + Cake.
Quick Test
Q1. How many chromosomes in a human mitotic daughter cell? → 46 (diploid, 2n).
Q2. In which stage do chromosomes line up in the middle? → Metaphase.
Q3. What separates in anaphase? → Sister chromatids (each becomes its own chromosome).
Q4. What is cytokinesis? → Division of the cytoplasm into two daughter cells.
Q5. Where does mitosis NOT happen? → In germ cells (sperm/egg formation uses meiosis).
